title: The Science of Extraction: Why Your Espresso Tastes Sour
summary: Struggling with sour or bitter coffee? We break down the mechanics of extraction so you can achieve the perfect balance every morning.
body:
The Extraction Spectrum

Espresso brewing is essentially a race against time and chemistry. Extraction refers to how much of the coffee solubles are dissolved into the water. When you pull a shot, the acids are extracted first, followed by sugars, and finally the heavy bitters.

The Sour Culprit: Under-Extraction

If your espresso tastes sharp, salty, or unpleasantly sour, you have likely under-extracted. This happens when the water hasn't had enough contact time or surface area to pull out the sugars. To fix this, try grinding finer or increasing your yield.

The Bitter End: Over-Extraction

Conversely, a dry, ashy, or intensely bitter shot is over-extracted. You've pulled out too many organic compounds. To remedy this, coarsen your grind or decrease the water temperature slightly.

Finding the Sweet Spot

The goal is the sweet spot—where acidity and bitterness balance each other out to reveal the bean's unique origin flavors.
